reason: Math inconsistency: question states 'assuming 4.5 persons/unit' but rationale calculation uses 5 occupants/unit. Also, question mentions 'average unit floor area of 28 sqm' (extraneous info) but calculation uses lot area (64 sqm). No road deduction applied in the rationale despite mentioning 30% roads. The question text and rationale need alignment.

proposed.text: A 1.5-hectare socialized single detached housing project has a minimum lot area of 64 sqm per unit. Calculate the gross density in persons/hectare assuming 5 persons/unit and no deduction for roads and amenities (gross density basis).

rationale.a: 1,042 persons/ha would require 1,042 × 1.5 = 1,563 persons, which is 313 units at 5 pax/unit, needing 20,000 sqm of lots — exceeds the 1.5 ha site.
rationale.c: 1,390 persons/ha would require 1,390 × 1.5 = 2,085 persons, needing 417 units at 5 pax/unit — not achievable on this site.
rationale.d: 500 persons/ha underestimates the density; actual density is higher given the lot area and occupancy assumptions.
rationale.correct: Units per hectare = 10,000 sqm ÷ 64 sqm/lot = 156.25 units/hectare. Gross density = 156.25 × 5 occupants = 781.25 ≈ 781 persons/hectare. Note: floor area is not used in gross density calculation; lot area determines unit count.
rationale.takeaway: Gross density = (site area ÷ lot area) × persons per unit ÷ site area in hectares. Floor area is not part of this calculation.
